concerns.text: The plan states that descriptor computation will be deterministic but does not provide a justification that the chosen set of descriptors (mixing entropy, atomic size mismatch, electronegativity variance, VEC, melting‑temperature variance) fully captures the physics of yield strength; without a cited basis the construct validity of the predictors is uncertain.

Permutation importance is described as being computed with 1 000 permutations per feature and significance assessed via a two‑tailed t‑test. The t‑test assumes normality of the permutation‑importance scores, which is not guaranteed; a non‑parametric test (e.g., permutation‑based p‑value) would be more appropriate.

The plan does not clarify whether permutation importance is evaluated on the held‑out test set or on the same data used to train the final model. Computing importance on the training data can inflate importance scores and constitute data leakage.

The dataset size (≈ 1 200 alloys) is claimed to give > 80 % power to detect an R² ≥ 0.6, but no formal power analysis is presented—only a deferred placeholder. A concrete power calculation (or citation) is required to justify the sample size.

The cross‑validation strategy is described as 5‑fold CV, yet the split between CV folds and the final held‑out test set is not explicitly defined. Without a clear separation, there is a risk of information leakage between model selection and final evaluation.
